title: The Vietnam War
subject: histoire
description: For twenty years the United States poured enormous force into Vietnam to hold back communism. It got bogged down, tore itself apart, and left without winning.

hero.hook: The world's leading power against a war it could not win.

blocks.text: At the heart of the Cold War, Vietnam split in two. A communist regime in the North. A Western-backed state in the South. The United States sent in enormous resources. Even so, it got stuck.
This conflict was not only military. It divided America, showed the limits of raw force, and left lasting scars on both sides.

sections.title: A divided country, then a war that grew

blocks.text: After the French defeat in the **[[Indochina War]]**, the Geneva Accords (**1954**) split Vietnam at the **17th parallel**. In the North, **[[Ho Chi Minh]]**, a nationalist and communist leader, took charge. In the South, an authoritarian regime backed by Washington.

The American presidents **John F. Kennedy** and then **Lyndon B. Johnson** feared the **[[domino theory]]**: if one country fell to communism, its neighbors would follow. In **August 1964** a naval incident in the Gulf of Tonkin served as a pretext to widen the war. By **1965**, Operation **[[Rolling Thunder]]** was bombing the North and the Marines were landing at Da Nang.

blocks.caption: American soldiers in Vietnam: a war of attrition in the jungle

blocks.text: Johnson is said to have remarked in private after Tonkin: “For all I know, our navy was shooting at whales out there.”

In **1969** about **543,000** American soldiers were in the country. The **[[search and destroy]]** strategy, hunting the enemy in order to wipe him out, and total air superiority still failed to cut the North Vietnamese supplies coming down the Ho Chi Minh trail. General **Vo Nguyen Giap**, the North's military chief, counted on constant harassment and on the support of part of the population.

The Americans also used defoliants such as Agent Orange to clear the jungle. The human and political cost exploded. The coffins came home. The **[[Pentagon]]**, headquarters of the American military, was learning that local political will can hold out against technology.
More than **80 million** liters of herbicide were sprayed, destroying about **20%** of the forests of South Vietnam.

sections.title: The shock of the Tet Offensive

blocks.text: On **January 30, 1968**, during the Vietnamese New Year, the **[[Tet Offensive]]** hit more than **100** cities. On the ground it was a failure for the North. On American television it was a shock: the “victory around the corner” promised by Washington now looked like a lie.

President **Richard Nixon** then launched “Vietnamization”: pull the American troops out while arming the South. The Paris Accords (**1973**) sealed the American departure. With no protector left, Saigon, the capital of the South, collapsed within two years.

sections.title: The end of the war, and what it left behind

blocks.text: On **April 30, 1975**, Saigon fell. About **58,000** Americans had died. Vietnamese losses ran into the millions. The first truly televised war, it also exposed crimes such as the massacre at **[[My Lai]]**, where American soldiers killed civilians in **1968**. America came out of it far more wary of distant interventions.

blocks.text: After **20 years** of war the United States left Vietnam without a victory: military power checked by politics, the country reunified under communism, and American society divided for decades.
